# OLYMPUS v0.0.21 build sheet (as written before the build, 2026-11-16, with §16 added after it)

> The round's build sheet kept whole as the contract the roles built to; **§16, as built, wins over any line above it that it contradicts.** DESIGN.md's log of 2026-11-16 carries the decisions. Where the sheet names a `// (v0.0.21 …` anchor, the release's strip removes them from `src/`.

# OLYMPUS v0.0.21, "Stack and clear: a house you have not seen, never a dead end, and what done means": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-16 for the round's four implementers (A, B, C, D) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on v0.0.20 as `.run/v020-design/sheet.md` gives it, which sits on v0.0.19 as `.run/v019-design/full/sheet.md` gives it. Where a release as built differs from its sheet, the code decides and the role says so in its handoff.

Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections it cites, then the three lens notes it merges (`.run/v021-design/house.md`, `done.md`, `perf.md`; each item below names its source as H*n*, D*n* or P*n*, and "as designed" means the mechanism, constants and tests there stand unless this sheet changes them). My own choices are marked (my call). Every conflict between the three notes, and between them and v0.0.19 and v0.0.20, is settled in §0.

**Lines.** The lenses measured on three different trees: the house lens on a snapshot of main mid v0.0.19 integration (`tree/` and its variants), the done lens on the v0.0.18 tag (main held a conflict marker in bundle.js then), the perf lens on a copy of main taken at 02:30 plus a prototype (`perf-proto.patch`, 132 lines). v0.0.19 and v0.0.20 move every one of their lines. So **every hunk is named by its function**, and a line is only a pointer.

**Verified for this sheet** (2026-11-16, read-only on main's working tree):
- `tests/house-fumble.test.mjs`: `KNOWN` holds 2 entries (`stoppage-silent`, `noshoot-silent`, :75 to :86), `OPEN` 5 (`pin-v018`, `p12-unready-v018`, `leads-on-v018`, `n7-rifle-up`, `pingpong-v018`, :95 to :106), `UNCOVERED` 1 (the dropped P-12, :109). D2's count stands.

H3's finding stands.

**The release.** The shoot house stays the pilot (the user, 2026-11-11: "This mission should be perfected before you spend any token on any other mission or core game mission, since most of the game will be basically this"). v0.0.18 made the options follow the gun and brought the kit; v0.0.19 the rest of the kit, the team and the live men; v0.0.20 what a player meets in every lane. v0.0.21 is the round that makes the house a test you cannot learn by heart, that closes every dead end on record, and that says what done is:

1. **The drawn house (A)**: three authored rooms placed by the seed on either side of the hall, each door push or pull with its latch toward you, found closed, open or locked, each room bringing its own men, every lane fair. "As set" stays on the picker and is the tests' default. This answers the user's ask of 2026-11-15: "doors should have a direction they open (pull or push) and it should affect our options for entry".
2. **Every lane holds (B)**: the four dead ends the drawn layouts found, the fumble net's last eight entries emptied, ownership by where a man stands, the #2's routing storm capped, and the gauges on 100 drawn lanes.
3. **Done (C)**: the acceptance list as data, the house's six acceptance moments, the ladder and the standards held, "qualified" on drawn seeds, a clean room counted for the career.
4. **The hand-off and the page (D)**: the drill, the team and the breach wherever a team meets a room plan; the gauges as a library; the page quiet in stop motion, the bakes sliced, a long session flat; the house on the bench card and on Windows.

Before all four, **stage 0 (the lead)** lands everything that moves no tick: the sim's busiest tick halved (P1, P3), the 2 ms rule as a test (P4), the quick suite's honest guards (P5), and the seams every role builds on (`opOf`, `two.js`, `houseSpecOf`, ownership by geometry).

**Merge order**: stage 0, then A, B, D, C. B's second half needs A's layouts, so B rebases onto A's merge (§3 step 10). C reads every role's tests and gauges (the acceptance list), so it merges last.

**Ship rules** (my call):
- Stage 0 and items 5 to 26 of §1 ship in v0.0.21.
- **The drawn house** (items 1 to 4, A) ships as `&draw=drawn` and the picker's switch if `house-assemble`, `house-cases`, `house-shapes`, `house-swings`, `house-door-states`, `house-fair`, `house-drawn-fixes` and `house-drawn-quick` are green at B's merge. Otherwise none of the drawn branch is reachable (the seam stays, the set is untouched) and it leads v0.0.22.
- **The default flips** to "drawn from the seed" (`HOUSE_DRAW_DEFAULT` 'drawn') only if `house-drawn` (heavy, 100 seeds × 4 bots, the kit slice and the fuzz) is green on the lead's quiet-machine run after the last merge **and** the user has answered question 3 yes (v0.0.20's question 16 default, "drawn, once the gauges hold on 100 drawn lanes", covered the cast, the places, the door states and the swings, not the rooms placed by the seed, which the hub's handcrafted rule makes the user's call: §0 item 52). Otherwise it ships 'set' with the switch one row away, and the announcement says why.
- **Mirrored rooms** (item 27, A, behind `MIRROR_ROOMS` false) turn on at the last merge only if `house-cases`' 8 mirror cases and a 40-seed mirror slice of `house-drawn` are green; else they ship off.
- **Qualified** (item 9, C) shows only if the drawn house ships (it qualifies on drawn seeds whatever the default).

**What the user must feel.**
- "Stack and clear" drawn from the seed is a house you have not cleared: the corner room first, south of the hall, its door a pull you cannot kick; the instructor says "Pull door, hinge right."; your #2 hooks where he crossed yesterday.
- A door already open at the start: nobody turns before GO. A locked push door: Kick or Pry, as you carry.
- The hostage may be in any room, or none; every room has a man to shoot; your #2's sector never holds two.
- Fumble the MAKE READY and sit: "Shooter, your pistol too: a round up." (built), and if the tower still moves on, "Your pistol. A round up." and "P-12 COLD" on the paper, never a cold P-12 found silently at the first jam. Stop with the P-12 out: MAKE SAFE holsters it. Fumble a draw or a holster: the words say where it is, every time (the floor only on question 13's answer).
- Three GOs in a row on houses you have never seen: "QUALIFIED: SERGEANT", and the picker offers "Qualify as Raider".
- In stop motion, the page does nothing while you think; at "Rifle, far left!", no hitch.
- "Stack and clear" played for an evening, "Again" after "Again": as quick at the twentieth as at the first.

**The user's rules hold over every section:** we only know what we know (the drawn house's code is shown on the card and the score line, never its cast before the lane); never a dead end; nothing pops in or out of view; AZERTY labels on physical codes; every image and sound by code; one loadout for every sheet; no overlapping UI; the look chosen from numbered samples the user scores; the standard lane ("as set") is v0.0.20's to the byte unless this sheet names the change (§0 item 51: it names none for the honest and keys bots).

**Kept as built and starred:** "Bang" (100, 100, 100, 2026-11-15) and its four B goldens; "Pairs" (100, 2026-11-08); "Three bangs" (100); hit card B (★ 99); P3-j's band (★ 100); the tower's macros (`src/sim/arms/macros.js`, re-exported by drills.js) and their words, item 6's holster riding on MAKE SAFE through `sidearm.js ADMIN` (the P-12's share of the tower's macros), never in macros.js; the row ids every bot, the instinct and the gauges key on; HOUSE1's, WHEEL_S4's, the C0 grid's and X4_PLANS' goldens (`04447e988e6958`, `05f066607e544d`, `1dd12b42226e54`, `1aed1872708ea3`); F1 to F59, never loosened.

**Rules of the round:**
- Edit only your own files and named hunks (§2). Report any other edit needed, exactly, in your handoff.
- No commits, tags, pushes, releases or promotions. Never touch `.play/`, :8200, :8201, `../longhaul` or `../tradecraft`.
- Scratch goes under `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v021/<role>/`. Your handoff goes in `.run/v021/<role>.md` (it survives a reboot): CHANGELOG bullets, doc text, the figures before and after, the pin's moved cells with the item that moved each (§3 step 10), every edit outside your list, the stubs you tested against.
- Worktrees: `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v021-<role> v0.0.20`, then `git -C <wt> apply .run/v021/stage0.patch`. The roles start only once v0.0.20 is tagged and its worktrees are removed, so 8230 to 8233 are free.
- Four roles share the machine: the runner with `JOBS=2`, and only `QUICK=1` or a file with its separator (`'house-fair ›'`). From stage 0 the runner scales its wall limit by 7/JOBS and guards CPU per file (P5), so a merge no longer "fails on time alone" at a small pool. Heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet-machine run (§9). While `lsof -nP -iTCP:8200 -sTCP:LISTEN` answers and the Mac has had input in the last 5 minutes, `JOBS=1`.
- A quick file stays under `QUICK_FILE_CPU_S` 3 s × k of CPU; from stage 0 the runner fails it, and no new file may join `QUICK_SLOW`.

**Ports:** A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233, reviews 8234 and 8235, the lead 8239 (stage 0 and the integration; `OLYMPUS_TEST_PORT` for single browser suites; the runner claims 8240 to 8249 itself). Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first.** Each role writes §4's exports as stubs with the shapes given, then fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges. Stage 0 writes the seams' set branches, so every reader already works on layout A.

**Integration.** As v0.0.20's: the stage-0 tree is the base, `B=$(cat .run/v021/base.tree)`; each role's patch is

```
git -C <wt> add -N . && git -C <wt> diff $B > .run/v021/<role>.patch
```

but for B, whose patch is cut against the tree A's merge left (`.run/v021/after-A.tree`, §3 step 9). The lead applies them with `git apply --3way` in the merge order, running `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each. Before its final run, each role rebases onto the integrated tree the roles before it left.

One helper, `readKey(s)`, is `${tick}|${ms}|${inputSeq}` while the clock is held (`inputSeq` bumped with every non-empty input main.js posts) and `${tick}|${seq}|${ms}` while it moves; every memo of main.js keyed on `clock.seq` (the ten of the verified list: `readSim`, `houseRead`, `contactRead`, `suppRead`, the bundle, the strip, AVPU, the plaque, pairs, stress) takes it in place of `seq`, each keeping its own extra fields (`readSim`'s stop fields). With stage 0's held second, nothing in the sim or the page is rebuilt in a long pause (today 0.82 ms mean, 3.35 max a held tick).

13. **The busiest tick** (stage 0; P1, P3, P4). The read scope `state.$reads` (opened by `instinctStep`, `instinctAction` and `stepsOf` when none is open; closed in a `finally`): `stepsOf` once per ms, `bodyOf` once per person and ms; `record.js readFull` with the non-enumerable `FULL` mark read by `stagesOf`, `pEffOf` and cues.js's three other `withDefaults(body)` reads; the held second due once; `READS_FREEZE=1` (set by the runner for the quick suite) deep-freezes what the scope memoises; `houseNow`'s `sheet`, `summary` and v0.0.20's `debrief` as lazy getters; `runHouse` ending on `state.armoury.range.end`; the bots reading `houseNow` once a tick. Measured: tier one 48213 3.12 → 1.25 ms, flash 5.88 → 1.40, breach 5.57 → 1.41, private 2.26 → 1.01; the twelve slowest house quick files 58.7 → 34.6 s wall; every digest unchanged. The prototype is re-applied by function onto v0.0.20, whose new readers (the cold Fix, the masked hold, the call-outs) run inside the scope: a write in one throws under the freeze, and is the reader's bug.

The recruit's fuzz on 1185 spends 29,007,687 nodes in one lane today.

## 3. Stage 0 (the lead, on v0.0.20's tag, port 8239, before the roles start)

Every step is byte-identical: `house-pin`'s 24 cells, `'house-flawless-quick ›'` and `'house-flawless-keys ›'` give v0.0.20's figures, and every digest of perf.md's list (`perf-tools/digest.mjs`) is the same. Step 2's quick cut changes which lanes the quick suite runs, not any lane.

0. **What v0.0.20 shipped**: the lead reads v0.0.20's CHANGELOG and notes in `.run/v021/lead.md` whether its voice (item 7) and plan view (item 26) shipped under their rules. If the plan view did not, `house-debrief.js` does not exist and §0 item 25 is void; if the voice did not, item 12's voice half applies to the Standby line and the call-outs only as built.
1. **The busiest tick** (item 13): perf-proto.patch re-applied by function onto v0.0.20, with `READS_FREEZE`, the `$reads` writer scan (`state.$reads` written only in instinct.js and shooting.js), `reads-scope`, `tests/tick-costs.mjs` (`tickCosts(lane, { runs: TICK_RUNS })`), `house-tick-budget` (quick: tier one 48213 by T and the private 48213 by the keys), `house-tick-budget-more` (heavy), and `house-live-perf` asserting the min-of-three maximum. F60 is enforced from here but for the fuzz clause, which B's item 14 brings in (printed until then), and for the live clause until this step measures it: perf.md measured the live lanes on the base only (3.31, 3.64, 2.33 and 3.16 ms) and did not prototype the fix there, so the lead measures them after the re-apply, and a live lane still over 2 ms × k is a stage-0 finding traced (in `.run/v021/lead.md`) and fixed before the roles start, never a budget moved.
2. **The quick suite** (item 26): the runner, the cut, `QUICK_SLOW` frozen from this step's measure plus 25%, `QUICK_CPU_S` set from the first whole run, both printed in `.run/v021/lead.md`.
3. **The operation record** (item 21's stage-0 half): op.js, every read through it, the cqb.js gates by kind, `lockedOf` through `brokenOf`, the `OP_HOME` scan.
4. **The #2's brain** (item 21): `house-two.js` moved to `src/sim/combat/two.js` byte for byte; `shoothouse.js` registers its host at load; `house-two.js` kept one release as a re-export shim (old imports in tests resolve; my call), deleted in v0.0.22; the scan that no file of `src/sim/combat/` imports from `src/sim/scenarios/`; `import-order` loads op.js, two.js, assemble.js and shoothouse.js first, each in a fresh process (two.js importing the host's functions lazily through `hostOf`, so no top-level read crosses the old cycle, v0.0.19 §0 item 12).
5. **The house seam** (H1): `assemble.js`'s set branch, every reader through `houseSpecOf` and `planSetOf`, `standsOf(state)` taking the state, `house-spec` (the import scan, §0 item 47) and `house-assemble`'s set case ("the set's spec, area and plans are HOUSE1, WHEEL_S4 and X4_PLANS.A, the same objects").
6. **Ownership by geometry** (item 8's plumbing).
7. **`createGame`'s `draw` and `house`** (§0 item 50): passed to the fill; `draw` 'set' by default; `house` a code, used only with `draw: 'drawn'` or alone (it implies drawn).
8. **The anchors**, one comment line per role, separated by at least one unchanged line, each `// (v0.0.21 <role>)`: cqb.js's rule list (B's, before `cqb-door`); courses.js `HOUSE_CHIEF` (A, then B); `tests/house-fumble.test.mjs` `KNOWN` and `OPEN` (B's deletions only, but an unchanged line between each pair of adjacent entries, as v0.0.20's stage 0 did, so B's patch applies cleanly over any v0.0.20 fixture lines; B deletes by id as the file stands after v0.0.20: v0.0.20's sheet names `pin` and `cold-fix` in `KNOWN`, which the v0.0.18 tag had already fixed and removed, house-fumble.test.mjs:76 to 78, so its deletions may be empty); `tests/syntax.test.mjs`' rule list (stage 0's own). The lead deletes them before the release.
9. **The saves**: two v0.0.20 saves in `tests/saves/`, gzipped, made by v0.0.20's code, with their `game-upgrade` cases: the private by the keys at a contact's pause in room 2 (the voice's queue and the masked hold over it; the read scope and the op seam load over it), and the sergeant at the tower's Stop with the P-12 drawn (item 6 loads over it: B's `house-pistol` reads it). No honest or keys set lane reaches Stop with the P-12 drawn, and v0.0.17's pistol save played by its own bot (`stoppageBot({ answer: 'transition' })`) presses Rifle up before Stop (measured: holstered at Stop, 2,710 ticks to the card), so the recipe is that save played by the same bot with Rifle up refused (`weapon:rifle-up` never chosen), to the tower's Stop's first pause, checked to hold the P-12 in the hand; the recipe is written in its `game-upgrade` case.
10. **The base tree and the patch**, as v0.0.20's (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=.run/v021/idx git add -A; git write-tree > .run/v021/base.tree`, `.run/v021/stage0.patch`). After A's merge, the lead writes `.run/v021/after-A.tree` the same way, and B cuts its patch against it.
11. **The pin, at every merge.** `house-pin`'s 24 cells (18 honest, 2 keys, 4 kit; no fuzz cell) hold at every merge, B's included (§0 item 51); the fumble net's fixtures move by item 7 and fuzz lanes by item 14, each printed with its item in `.run/v021/lead.md`. A moved pin cell stops the merge. `house-pin-drawn` is recorded at B's merge and holds after.

## 4. Interfaces

### 4.0 stage 0

```js
// op.js
opOf(state) → record | null        // the house: state.armoury.range.house (the same object); else state.cqb ?? null
opLive(state) → bool                // the house: inHouse(state) && laneLive(R); else !!state.cqb && its area is the player's
registerHost(course, host); hostOf(state) → host   // host: { noteSighting, shot, say, legOf, … }; off the lane NULL_HOST
brokenOf(state, openingId) → ms | null; breakOpening(state, openingId, atMs)   // the house: R.house.broken; else the delta (D)
// assemble.js (the set branch)
houseSpecOf(state) → HOUSE1 on the set; planSetOf(state) → X4_PLANS.A on the set; houseCodeOf(state) → 'A' | code
assembleHouse(code) → null; registerHouse(code) → null    // A fills
// two.js: every export of house-two.js, unchanged
// tests/tick-costs.mjs
tickCosts(lane, { runs = TICK_RUNS }) → { maxMs, p50, p95, top: [{ tick, ms, facts }] }
// tests/game.mjs
createGame({ …, draw = 'set', house = null })
```

**State**: `state.$reads` (runtime Map; `builds` counted); `T.slot` written from `sectorOf` (equal to today's on the set).

### 4.1 A

```js
// chunks/x4.js
X4_CHUNKS[c] = { rooms, openings, socket, plans: { [family]: plan }, stands: [{ role, letter, face, trigger, gapMs?, places: [{ x, z, why }] }], family(how, mirror) }
// assemble.js
assembleHouse(code) → { area, spec, plans }; registerHouse(code) → area; generatedArea(id); generatedOpening(id)
drawHouse(seed, { doors = 'drawn', mirror = MIRROR_ROOMS } = {}) → layout code     // never reads the loadout; the fill appends |f…|p…
layoutPartOf(code) → the three rooms' part; areaIdOf(code) → 'melas.wheel.s4~' + hash('house', layoutPartOf(code)).toString(16).padStart(8, '0').slice(0, 7)   // core/hash.js hash is 32-bit
// model.js (A): registerArea(area), dropArea(id) (the registry, read by areaOf, openingOf, openingArea)
SHAPES (runtime cache, golden), HOUSE_DRAWS (the codes of seeds 1 to 100, golden)
// shoothouse.js
drawStands(seed, spec = null)        // spec null: the set's draw, byte for byte
// courses.js: draws.doors, draws.cast by chunk
```

**State** (absent on the set): `R.house.draw = { mode: 'drawn', v: 1, code }`; `state.places.live.gen = { base, code, v: 'assemble@1' }`; the open doors' deltas at the fill; `R.house.intel` as built (`intelOf` over the drawn turners).

### 4.2 B

```js
// route.js
routed(state, pts, { area, open = [], bodies = [], cap } = {})   // v0.0.20's signature plus cap; fail: 'cap' | 'blocked'
ROUTE_NODES_TICK 8000
// bundle.js
OFF_PATH_RETRY_MS 500, OFF_PATH_MOVED_M 0.05
// two.js
releaseHolds(state, H, leg)
// plan.js
dryPick(state, pid) → gunId | null   // latched on state.stop.dryPick
// shoothouse.js
houseMoveOn(state, bus) → void     // from handling.js moveOn on the house course: H.pistolCold and the line, once
// sidearm.js
ADMIN.safe = 'pistol:holster'       // MAKE SAFE's P-12 share; adminSubs(state, pid, 'safe') for a drawn P-12
// courses.js
HOUSE_CHIEF.pistol = ['Your pistol. A round up.']   // the move-on's; HOUSE_NUDGE.pistol (30 s) as built
```

**State** (absent by default): `state.$route = { seq, nodes, failed }` (runtime); `rec.offPathFail = { ms, x, z, pathKey }` on the #2's move record; `state.stop.dryPick`; `H.pistolCold`.

### 4.3 C

```js
houseVerdict(state, { standard = sheetStandard(state) } = {}) → { go, why: [] }
cleanRoomOf(state, leg) → bool; drillRep(state, pid, family, { clean, teacher, field }) → rung
DONE: [{ id, group, what, words?: { date, text }, check: { kind: 'test' | 'gauge' | 'moment' | 'sample' | 'user', ref }, by?, answered? }]
MOMENTS: [{ id, title, start: { tier, seed, setup, loadout, scenario, draw: 'set' }, bot, holds, prints }]
LADDER_LANE_K 0.02, LADDER_TAKEIN_MS 25, LADDER_FIRST_MS 30, GO_OWN_MIN 0.90, NOGO_UP_MIN 0.80
QUAL_GOS 3, QUAL_LOADOUTS ['standard'], QUAL_DRAW 'drawn'
REPS_PRACTISED 20, REPS_DRILLED 60, FIELD_REP_K 2, FIELD_REPS_SOL 5, THINK_S 6, DEAD_AIR_GAP_S 15, DEAD_AIR_MAX 0.20, SAVE_HOUSE_KB 200
```

**State**: none in the sim (the pars written at load are v0.0.20's fields). `localStorage['olympus.house']` gains `code` on a run, `qual: { n, of }`, and `quals` (UI only).

### 4.4 D

```js
openOp(state, { area, team }); closeOp(state)       // state.cqb = { area, asked, read, order, team, bursts, broken }
setOpening(state, id, s, { atMs, how, broken })     // v0.0.20's plus broken (off the lane only)
watch(game, { team, plans, area }) → { tick(game), result() }   // cqb-gauges.mjs: walls, bodies, swings, pins, lines, corners, entry
BAKE_CHUNK_SAMPLES 4096, BAKE_SLICE_MAX_MS 5, UPLOAD_MID_KB 64, BENCH_HOUSE_KIT_S 25, SOAK_GROWTH_MB 8
```

**State**: `state.cqb` (off the lane only, never null-written); main.js's `inputSeq` (page only).

**Tick order** (v0.0.20's, unchanged): `houseActors` runs the #2's runSlot and `twoTick` (now two.js's), `opforTick` (L), the instructor's walk; then `houseRules`: `readsTick`, L's covering, v0.0.20 A's `maskTick`, C's `traceTick` last. B's route budget resets on the tick's first `routed` call (`$route.seq !== tick`). Decisions act the next tick.

## 10. Risks (each owned)

- **A drawn lane meets a dead end no bot has** (B): the fuzz and the net run drawn slices, the default flips only on `house-drawn`, and the lead files each new mechanism in `.run/hunt-findings.json`.
- **The drawn house is the round's L** (A): stage 1 has 36 shapes and a prototype that rebuilt layout A field for field; the mirrors are behind their own switch; if A is red at B's merge, the drawn branch is unreachable and the set is untouched (the ship rule).
- **The stage-0 refactors are wide** (lead): about 100 read sites through `opOf`, 21 through `houseSpecOf`, the #2's module moved, the perf patch re-applied onto v0.0.20's new readers. Each is byte-identical by construction and checked by the pin, the digests and the scans; a moved cell stops stage 0, and the step is redone, never patched round.
- **The read scope hands one object to several readers** (lead): `READS_FREEZE` in the quick suite throws on the first write; v0.0.20's readers are its likeliest offenders.
- **B depends on A** (B, lead): B's first half (items 6, 7, 14) needs only stage 0; its second rebases on A's merge; the lead writes `after-A.tree` the hour A lands.
- **SHAPES grows by combinations** (A): 22 to 23 ms for three chunks without mirrors, 127 ms with them (the prototype); a fourth chunk about 4 times as many; over 500 ms, the list becomes data with a golden.
- **The rooms placed by the seed against the handcrafted rule** (lead): §0 item 52's reading is my call; the default flips only on the user's yes to question 3, and "as set" stays one row away whatever they answer.
- **The stage's build of a new area at each fill** (A): measured nowhere yet in the page; `ui-house-drawn` against `AREA_BUILD_MS` 250, and the build runs behind the brief's splash.
- **A session's caches** (A, D): every code feeds five caches; `HOUSE_REG_KEEP` and the stage's eviction, held by `ui-soak`.
- **The kit on drawn lanes** (A, B): the frag's brief and the BC-1's stand-off are set-shaped (§0 items 32, 33); `house-drawn`'s kit slice is their check.
- **The quick suite's new guards fail roles at first** (lead): `QUICK_SLOW` is frozen at stage 0 from a measure, so no existing file fails; a role's new quick file over 3 s × k is moved to heavy, never added to the list.
- **The default's flip changes the user's house under their fingers** (lead): only under the ship rule, with "as set" one row away on the picker, said in the announcement; question 3 asks again.
- **The moments' estimates** (C): rewriting COMBAT §25.10.4 from the measure (my call) could hide a slow lane; F71's dead-air half stays strict.
- **The working tree's lines** (every role): every hunk is named by function.

## 13. For the user

**The questions, each built with its default:**

1. **The bar.** Is the shoot house "perfected" when you star "Stack and clear" (and "Stack and clear, live"), or at a number on every aspect (70, 90)? *Default: your star on both, with every machine check of the acceptance list green on the same release.*
2. **Hinges against the approach.** Should a door's hinge be drawn on either end, so some stacks form beyond their door and your #2 leads past it ("the crossing")? Or should the latch always face the way you come, with push or pull, the side of the hall and the room's shape varying? *Default: the latch toward you. Today every lane stalls when the stack forms beyond its door: your #2 held 361.5 s behind you.*
3. **The drawn house by default.** Your rule of 2026-11-05 is that the world is handcrafted, "game world is handcrafted", so nothing in a place's layout is rolled per career. The shoot house's rooms are panels the instructors move (PLACES §4.12's layouts A, B and C), so I read a house drawn per lane, inside house 1's fixed walls, hall and catwalk, as an exercise's detail, not a new place. Should "Stack and clear" then place its three rooms by the seed (36 arrangements, 95 different houses in 100 seeds) as well as draw the cast, the places, the door states and the swings that v0.0.20's question 16 asked about, and be "drawn from the seed" by default once 100 drawn lanes meet every gauge, with "as set" (the house you have played) on the picker? *Default: built and on the picker; the default stays "as set" until you say yes.*
4. **Mirrored rooms.** The rooms flipped along the hall too, bringing two new entries (the corner room crossed, the L to its left), 304 layout shapes against 36? *Default: yes, once the first stage holds.*
5. **Doors found open or locked.** A lane door open 25% of the time and locked 15% (push doors only: kicked or pried)? *Default: yes.*
6. **The hostage anywhere.** At most one a lane in any room, sometimes none, or always in the L's far leg as now? *Default: drawn, at most one.*
7. **Three rooms always**, or two to four (new rooms written first)? *Default: three this round.*
8. **Furniture** (tables, beds, cabinets), or bare rooms as most shoot houses are? *Default: bare until you say.*
9. **Qualified.** Three GOs in a row on three seeds the game draws and hides, never played on that sheet, on the drawn house, standard kit, your sheet's par or harder? Or three of four? *Default: three in a row.*
10. **The tier one's standard.** He shares the Raider's operator par (0.8 s); his first round averages 655 ms against the Raider's 738. His own (0.7 s), so a GO as Raider is not a GO as tier one? *Default: shared, as built.*
11. **The moments.** "Step by step, as a private", "Clean, as tier one", "The jam in room 2", "Bang, then go", "Through the hinges", "A man, not a stand": the stretches that prove it to you? And a seventh on a drawn house? *Default: these six, on the house as set.*
12. **After the close.** The parked environment round, then 0.0.7e "Hold to hold" at micro-g as ROADMAP orders; or 0.0.7f "Bang, then go" first, since its men are built in the pilot? *Default: ROADMAP's order.*
13. **The dropped P-12.** When a draw or a holster is fumbled: on the floor with a "Pick up" row (1.2 s), or, as v0.0.18 built it, the words say where it stayed ("snags in the holster: it stays in.", "misses the holster: still in your hand.")? *Default: the words, as built, now checked against the truth on every lane.*
14. **The 2 ms rule** measured as the busiest tick, each tick's own cost the least of three runs of the same lane, the p95 printed beside it? *Default: yes.*
15. **The quick suite's minute.** 60 s at the full pool of 7 workers, the wall limit scaled by 7/JOBS when the pool is smaller, guarded by CPU budgets (3 s a file, 200 s the suite), and the whole-lane cases moved to the heavy suite (each keeping one or two seeds quick, its name saying where the rest went)? *Default: yes.*
16. **From Windows**, `play.cmd --dev`: would you paste the cards of `?bench=shoothouse`, `house-kit`, `house-live` and `house-stop`? And which machine is it (CPU, GPU, display refresh rate)?

## 16. As built, and where it departed from the sheet (2026-11-16)

**The order.** Stage 0 on the v0.0.20 snapshot (9c65bcd, base tree `00829189…`); A, B (rebased on A), D and C in worktrees; the merges A, B, D, C by `git apply --3way` over v0.0.20's tag with the post-snapshot closers; two reviews and two fixers; the integrator's hand edits; a play review and a code review and one fixer; the two sample sets. The handoffs are in `.run/v021/` (`lead.md`, `a.md`, `b.md`, `c.md`, `d.md`, `integrate.md`, `fix.md`).

**Built as the sheet says.** Items 1 to 26 (the drawn house with its doors, states and cast; the four dead ends; the P-12 at the tower; the net emptied; ownership by geometry; qualified; the ladder and standards; the quiet page; sliced bakes; the 2 ms rule; the routing cap; the long session; the card's code and "Again"; the gauges on drawn lanes; the goldens, the drawn pin and the drawn save; the six moments; the acceptance list; the operation off the range; the bench card's house benches; the gauges as a library; the clean room; pars at load; the quick suite's guards). F60 to F73.

**Departures and settlements** (each recorded in DESIGN.md's log or the handoff):
- **Item 27 (mirrored rooms) is not built**: `MIRROR_ROOMS` is false; the two new entries and `house-cases`' mirror cases wait for v0.0.22.
- **The default is not flipped**: `HOUSE_DRAW_DEFAULT` 'set'. `house-drawn` is red on F2, F4, F6, F10, F12 and F65 (the sweep) and eight rows of the kit slice (F4, F6, F7, F10, F12, F17, F25, F27); `house-swings`' F4 (a corner room last, north of the hall) is the same family. The picker's row and `&draw=drawn` ship.
- **`QUICK_CPU_S` is 375 × k, not the sheet's 200**: the machine's measured quick run is 288 to 446 s of CPU, and CPU time is not load-independent here; the per-file budget stays 3 s × k, 35 files in `QUICK_SLOW` frozen, and the budgets are judged at a load of at most half the cores.
- **F14 is closed** (the lane's due, v0.0.20's closer; `house-flawless-keys` MET on the merged tree) and removed from the acceptance list's OPEN gauges. **F70, F71 and F73 are OPEN** (the recruit's GO 25% and the sergeant at operator 30%; the private's 7.50 real minutes; a mid-lane band upload of 230 to 238 KB in the house-kit and house-live benches: `render/figures.js` should paint every band before GO, a file no role owned).
- **D's `opActors`, `opRules` and `opInput` are wired only by the tests** (`OP_WEAPONS`): no scene opens an operation yet, so wiring them into the weapons domain would run the layers in every game for nothing.
- **A drawn lane door's lock is unknown until read or tried** (the play review; the sheet had the lock known at the fill).
- **The cold P-12's words are v0.0.20's** (§4.2's `HOUSE_CHIEF.pistol`, "Your pistol. A round up.", and the paper's "P-12 COLD", `H.pistolCold`, are not built): the tower's move-on already racked an owed P-12 and said so ("Your pistol had no round up. I've racked it.", `HOUSE_CHIEF.pistolRacked`), kept as it was (`tests/house-pistol.test.mjs`' header).
- **Pars on drawn houses gain a `turn` part and the second man's start** (the play review); the raider by the honest bot 18 of 24 drawn houses, the corporal 20.
- **The area id numbers the layout one to one** (the code review; the sheet's 7-digit hash collided on 27 pairs in 150,000 seeds).
- **The integrator's hand edits**: `giveWay` (an exact equivalence, taken after the quiet-machine check: without it F60 was OPEN on three drawn lanes), the keys bot's two drawn-house rules held to drawn houses (re-stacking only at a door found open at the fill; the passed-point skip on a drawn house only), the fumble net's `end()` judging only due words, ui-finish sending an input before reading the card, the runner's `CEILING` matching `machineNow()`, `bangEntry` read through `opOf`, `cleanRoomOf` holding v0.0.20's paint rule. No gauge loosened.
- **Pins**: house-pin's 24 set cells are v0.0.20's tag's, unmoved by every merge and fix; house-pin-drawn re-recorded (the PA's drawn brief, B's keys bot, B's `cqb-contact` 'his' fix, the new ids, the locked door on 1037: 3963 → 3923, the keys private on 48213: 4762 → 4782), each cause in the file; house-shoot's standard rows re-pinned for the X label; house-drawn-fixes (d) now pins the second man's par met.
